title: Heat vs. Temperature
subcategory: Thermal Physics — Thermal Properties of Matter

references.label: NCERT Physics Part II, Class 11 — Thermal Properties of Matter

summary: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of a substance's particles. Heat is the energy transferred between systems because of a temperature difference.
explanation: Temperature is a state property — it describes the current condition of a system (how 'hot' it is on some scale). Heat, by contrast, is energy in transit: it only exists as heat while it's flowing from a hotter object to a cooler one, driven by the temperature difference between them. Once transferred, that energy becomes part of the receiving system's internal energy, not a stored quantity of 'heat.' Two objects can contain very different total thermal energy yet have the same temperature (e.g., a cup and a bathtub of water at the same temperature), since temperature doesn't depend on the amount of substance.

comparison.left: Temperature: average kinetic energy per particle
comparison.right: Heat: energy transferred due to temperature difference
Yes — heat transferred scales with mass

commonMisconceptions: Using 'heat' and 'temperature' interchangeably in casual speech, e.g. saying an object 'has a lot of heat' when it actually has high temperature or high internal energy.
genZNote: Temperature is a status update. Heat is the energy actually being sent between two systems.
